provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `Confessoris` where 1862 reads `Confess6ris`; 1962 reads `Domine, intercessionibus adiuvemur:` where 1862 reads `D6mine, intercessi6nibus adjuv6mur :`; 1962 reads `delinquendo offendimus,` where 1862 reads `delinqu6ndo off6ndimus,`; 1962 reads `meritis` where 1862 reads `m6ritis`; 1962 reads `precibus, nostrorum` where 1862 reads `pr6cibus, nostr6rum`; 1962 reads `veniam` where 1862 reads `v6niam`; 1962 has `Iesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.`; 1862 has nothing there; 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus; 1862 prints the j-orthography (adjuvemur, majestatem, ejus); 1862 conclusion is `Per Dominum nostrum.`; the 1962 writes it out in full; the CMAA layer reads an internal capital F in one word (`ofFendimus`), a broken serif; the 1862 and the Benziger both read it plainly and it was lower-cased mechanically. Corroboration: 1922 Mame carries 6 October at PDF p. 845; not transcribed, the 1862 settles the reading.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Sancti Brunonis Confessoris tui, quaesumus, Domine, intercessionibus
adjuvemur: ut, qui majestatem tuam graviter delinquendo offendimus, ejus
meritis et precibus, nostrorum delictorum veniam consequamur. Per Dominum
nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
